To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
perceived creative climate and perceived workload are important variables that can predict a large proportion of the variance in the dependent variable organizational creativity.

perceived creative climate has a strong positive correlation with organizational creativity, perceived workload has a moderate negative correlation with organizational creativity and sick leave has a negative correlation with organizational creative climate.
the perceived creative climate, perceived workload and sick leave are all important predictors for organizational creativity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between perceived organizational creativity, perceived creative climate, perceived workload and sick leave.
how to improve the work environment for HR-employees, and how to promote organizational creativity in the organization as a whole.
the importance of a perceived creative climate and perceived workload for organizational creativity and how this can be related to the employees' sick leave.

the study showed no significant differences in the four main variables between the private and public sector.
the study has shown that perceived creative climate and workload are important variables in relation to the organizational creativity among HR-employees.
there are no significant differences between the two sectors, which indicates that the results can be generalized to the entire HR-functions in Sweden.

the results indicate a strong relationship between perceived creative climates and organizational creativity.
a positive relationship between organizational creativity, perceived creative climate and workload was found.
